JustCo Place in Orchard secures 80% retail leasing commitment ahead of opening
article:
Co-working, co-living and retail development JustCo Place at 160 Orchard Road has secured leasing commitments for 80% of its retail podium as it gears up to debut the retail podium and co-living apartments in the coming months.

The retail tenant mix spans global brands, concepts that are new to Singapore or the region, and homegrown businesses in F&B, lifestyle and wellness.

Under the fitness and wellness offerings, the committed tenant line-up includes New York performance training brand AARMY; UK fitness brand Karve, which will focus on Pilates; Singapore martial arts name Evolve MMA Orchard’s flagship academy, which is taking up 10,000 sq ft; and hair salon SO Salon.

F&B players include Michelin Bib Gourmand Korean restaurant brand Gwanghwamun Mijin, Surrey Hills Grocer’s first flagship bakery The Hills Bakehouse, Shanghai’s minimalist specialty coffee brand M Stand, Chinese hotpot chain Chamoon Royale, social dining bar and bistro Helen’s, as well as 160 Coffeehouse, a new local coffee concept created for JustCo Place.

Meanwhile, entertainment tenants include homegrown KTV brand K.Star Karaoke, and an escape room by live entertainment firm Fever.

The line-up “reflects JustCo’s approach to curating concepts around how people increasingly work, live, connect and spend their time, while remaining relevant to the lifestyles of Singapore’s consumers”, said the Singapore-listed flexible workspace operator in a Nov 5 bourse filing.

At the Orchard property, retailers are set to progressively start operating from this December onwards.

The co-living component under the Just At brand is expected to open in 2027, with 123 fully furnished apartments across Levels 6 to 10. JustCo will operate this serviced apartment tower under an asset-light management contract signed with OG.

On Levels 3 and 4, the co-working centre opened in September with full occupancy.

“With the coworking centre fully occupied, strong progress in retail leasing and the development of Just At underway, the different parts of the ‘work, live, connect’ ecosystem are steadily coming together,” said Kong Wan Sing, CEO of JustCo.

The development, owned by OG , formerly housed Taste Orchard and OG’s department store.

title: Westin Residences Penang takes branded waterfront living to new heights on Gurney Bay, Penang
article:
Rising 69 storeys above the Gurney Bay waterfront in the north of George Town, Westin Residences Penang is poised to become the tallest residential tower in Penang. The 498-unit development by Macrovest Sdn Bhd is also the first Westin-branded residence in the country, pairing the hospitality brand’s wellness philosophy with the comfort and privacy of a private home.

The project, which is currently under construction, caught the attention of judges at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026, who conferred on it the Top Development (Northern Malaysia) title in the high-rise category.

Westin Residences Penang is located along the edge of Gurney Bay overlooking the Straits of Malacca. It comprises 165 two-bedroom units, 271 three-bedroom units, 57 four-bedroom units, and five units with five bedrooms or more.

The development is envisioned as a sanctuary above the city, integrating biophilic landscapes, elevated living spaces and wellness-focused amenities in keeping with the Westin brand.

A sculpted waterfront landmark

Designed by Penang-based architecture firm Arkitek Permata Sdn Bhd in collaboration with a renowned international design consultant from Singapore, SAA Architects Pte Ltd, the tower is oriented to capture panoramic views of the Straits of Malacca, the greenery of the park by the sea at Gurney Bay along Gurney Drive, and the silhouette of Penang Hill.

Its fluid facade takes its cue from the movement of the sea, creating a shifting play of light and shadow throughout the  day.

On the side facing the city, landscaped terraces and open communal spaces bring greenery into the living environment.

The podium is conceived as an extension of the neighbouring park, with landscaped decks and lifestyle amenities.

A defining feature is the sculptural porte-cochère framed by V-shaped columns, which together form a “W” that gives the development a distinctive presence along the waterfront.

Gardens with a sense of place

The landscape design by Penang-based landscape architecture firm Permata Green Sdn Bhd draws on two neighbouring influences: the tropical lushness of the Penang Botanic Gardens and the shoreline of the Straits of Malacca.

Inspired by atolls and archipelagos, the podium gardens feature meandering pebble-wash pathways and layered planting. Outdoor dining pavilions come with herb planters set into the benchtops, encouraging residents to gather.

At the ground level, emergency vehicle lanes were reimagined as open lawns reinforced with engineered drainage cells, while fitness islands and exercise stations are dotted along circuit loops.

The podium houses a 50m lap pool and a vitality pool, with surfaces finished in 12 shades of glass tiles to capture the shifting hues of the sea.

The curated landscaping honours the timeless legacy of Gurney Drive. Graceful aquatic monuments by the pool echo the majestic sculptures that historically lined the promenade at Gurney Drive in the old days. This is complemented by native granite that pays tribute to the original Penang Botanic Gardens quarry.

By integrating signature textures like traditional plaster, mosaic broken marble and classic terrazzo, the design revives the iconic aesthetic of the 1990s —evoking a deep sense of nostalgia that remains beautifully relevant within today’s modern concepts, which is also aligned with the Westin brand’s emphasis of wellness living.

In alignment with Marriott International’s global standards for the Westin brand, the landscape design prioritises ecological balance by pairing resilient local flora with an advanced rainwater harvesting irrigation system.

Built for the long term

Westin Residences Penang is targeting GreenRE Silver AA provisional certification by Malaysia’s Real Estate and Housing Developers Association. Its building envelope uses high-performance glazing and a double-roof configuration to reduce solar heat gain.

Together with LED lighting, regenerative lifts and energy-efficient air conditioners, the project is expected to improve operational carbon performance by about 12.9%.

Up on the roof, solar panels will generate clean electricity and ease the building’s reliance on the grid. Water-saving fittings are expected to cut residents’ water use by about 40%, while harvested rainwater keeps the gardens lush.

Around a third of the living spaces are designed for natural cross-ventilation, staying cool with less need for air conditioning.

As for residents, electric-vehicle charging infrastructure provision is about 53% of parking bays, supporting the transition towards low-carbon transportation.

With its blend of branded hospitality, site-responsive design and green features, Westin Residences Penang sets a new benchmark for waterfront living in Penang.

title: Park Regent rises as Kuala Lumpur's lakeside landmark
article:
At the water’s edge of the Central Lake in Desa ParkCity, Kuala Lumpur, the two towers of Park Regent open out like a pair of arms, embracing The Central Park beyond.

Completed in September 2023, the 505-unit freehold development is the first premium high-rise residential project in the 473-acre township, and the first joint venture between Malaysia’s ParkCity Group and Singapore’s CapitaLand Development .

Park Regent was named Top Development (Central Malaysia) and Top Luxury Development (Central Malaysia) in the high-rise category at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026.

“When we plan a new development in Desa ParkCity, we look beyond the asset’s value appreciation potential that we can bring to our customers,” says ParkCity Group CEO Datuk Joseph Lau.

“Many of them are not just purchasing a property; they are investing in a lifestyle, with the desire to be part of an inclusive community that emphasises sustainability and caters to multigenerational families as they grow and thrive.”

Sitting on a 5.6-acre site (about 2.3ha), the development has a gross development value of about RM1.08 billion (around $338.7 million). Its units range from 872 to 4,887 sq ft across six layouts, from one-bedroom units to four-bedroom homes.

Launched in July 2019 at an average of RM1,100 psf, Park Regent saw about 70% of its units taken up during a two-day priority sale. The remaining units were sold during construction, despite the Covid-19 lockdowns. Since completion, resale prices have appreciated by 40% to 50%, while rental yields range from 5% to 6%, according to the developer.

Bungalows in the sky

Designed by London-based Serie Architects with Singapore’s Multiply Architects, the two towers are only a single unit wide. Their cascading heights, rising to 53 storeys, frame a central green space that visually extends The Central Park and makes the site feel larger than it is.

Instead of long corridors, each pair of units shares a lift core with a private lobby. Units are laid out horizontally with wide frontages, maximising light, views and cross-ventilation. Larger homes have double balconies up to 3m deep, roomy enough for a six-seater dining table or a koi pond, with sunken planters that screen views between floors.

“Living in an era of compact households, we often forget the luxuries we used to have, such as roomy balconies to lounge in, ample storage, ventilation and light, a yard and a spacious kitchen,” says Lau. “Park Regent is a testament to thoughtful luxury.”

Renowned Singapore interior designer Peter Tay curated the communal spaces, including the Lantern Lobby, a soaring atrium wrapped in copper-toned latticed metalwork that glows like a lantern at night.

Nature by design

Rather than leave a bulky car park in plain view, the design conceals it within a landscaped podium that slopes towards the lake like a green hill, complete with a waterfall. At the top sits the Level 3A facilities deck, where the infinity pool is linked to a bio-pond planted with 10 species of aquatic plants, some found along the Central Lake, which naturally help keep the water clear.

The landscape by Singapore’s Coen Design International takes up about 55% of the site. Before construction began, 82.9% of the trees on site were tagged for preservation or transplanting, with most replanted after completion. This gave Park Regent a mature landscape from day one and helped local wildlife return.

Park Regent is also Green Building Index-certified. A 42.9kWp rooftop solar system generates about 53,000kWh of electricity a year for the common areas, while rainwater harvesting cuts potable water use for landscaping by 58%. More than 50 EV chargers are installed, and the lifts use face recognition to take residents straight to their floors.

Construction quality has also been recognised, with the project scoring 85.5 under the Building Quality Assessment System, the highest on record in Desa Park-City, and recently winning gold in the high-rise residential category at the FIABCI World Prix d’Excellence Awards 2026.

What’s next

ParkCity’s latest residential project in the township is ParkCity Residences, with 433 freehold homes across two towers. Beyond Desa ParkCity, the group recently launched ParkCity Damansara, a master-planned township in Petaling Jaya, and is preparing ParkCity Botanika in Puchong South.

“Beyond completing and handing over a development, ParkCity remains committed to the ongoing upkeep of its townships and shared spaces,” says Lau. “This long-term stewardship is central to The ParkCity Way.”

title: Lightwater Residences wins double honours for exclusive waterfront living in Penang
article:
On the waterfront at the gateway to Penang Island, Lightwater Residences offers a front-row seat to the Penang Bridge and the Penang Straits. Its two towers hold just 262 homes, with only five units per floor and private lift lobbies for every residence.

Developed by IJM Perennial Development, a joint venture between IJM Corporation Bhd and Singapore-based Perennial Holdings , the project picked up two awards at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026: Top Development (Northern Malaysia) and Top Luxury Development (Northern Malaysia), both in the high-rise category.

Designed for Penang’s luxury buyers, who seek privacy, prestige and lasting value, the project pairs serene, sanctuary-style living with easy access to retail and lifestyle hubs.

Located at The Light Waterfront Penang, Lightwater Residences is the latest residential phase of The Light City, a waterfront masterplan that also includes The Waterfront Shoppes, the Penang Waterfront Convention Centre and a five-star hotel.

The unit mix comprises 156 two-bedroom-plus-study units, 48 three-bedroom units, 56 three-bedroom-plus-study units and two units with five bedrooms or more. The first sale and purchase agreement was signed in February 2025.

The project has drawn local, regional and international buyers who value high-end waterfront living. As at end-September, 50 units in Tower A had been signed, a take-up rate of 38.2%. Tower B is being held back for a future launch, while sales efforts for Tower A continue through targeted marketing, invite-only private previews and overseas roadshows.

Quiet luxury

Designed by DP Architects with Veritas Architects, the two towers are oriented towards the water so that every home enjoys sea views from the living, dining and bedroom spaces. Floor-to-ceiling glazing and generous balconies bring the seascape indoors, while the unit arrangement minimises overlooking between neighbours.

Inside, the interiors by Beta Architects follow a philosophy of quiet luxury, where quality and craftsmanship take precedence over display. Natural marble, brushed brass, bronze mirrors and bespoke wall coverings are layered to create warmth and depth, complemented by custom metal accents, integrated lighting and bespoke joinery.

Achieving that standard was no small feat amid rising construction costs. To meet high market expectations without compromising on quality, the project, design, contracts and construction teams worked closely together. Proactive value management and strict quality control helped contain budget pressures while preserving the intended architectural integrity and living experience.

Resort living by the sea

The facilities draw inspiration from luxury resorts and boutique hotels. At the heart of the offering is the Sky Club, with a sky lounge, whisky lounge, cigar lounge, private dining suites and a jacuzzi, all with sweeping views of the waterfront. Spaces for working, exercising and entertaining are planned so that residents of all ages, from children to seniors, can enjoy them.

On the podium, the landscape by Landarc Associates is guided by an “Estuary Biophilia” concept inspired by the places where rivers meet the sea. A central swimming pool forms the focal point, with pathways branching out like waterways to a series of themed zones. These include a community garden, a Heliconia Garden, and a settlement zone with private decks, lawns and sunken sofa lounges. A mist garden with stepped seating creates a cooling microclimate, while vertical garden columns bring greenery up into the architecture. Families are catered for with outdoor fitness areas, children’s playgrounds and a wading pool.

Green and connected

Lightwater Residences has been awarded GreenRE Gold provisional certification. Homes are designed for natural cross-ventilation and daylight, cutting the need for air-conditioning and artificial lighting. Energy-saving lifts and LED lighting reduce power use, harvested rainwater keeps the gardens green, and water-saving fittings cut household water use. Green concrete was used in construction, low-VOC paints and adhesives help keep indoor air healthy, and EV charging points are provided for residents. Native plant species help cool the surroundings and support local biodiversity, while recycling bins encourage residents to sort their waste.

The location is equally compelling. Next to the Penang Bridge, the development offers easy access to George Town, Penang International Airport and the Bayan Lepas economic corridor, and is within walking distance of a station on the future Mutiara LRT line.

With its low-density layout, resort-style facilities and prime waterfront address, Lightwater Residences sets a new benchmark for luxury living in Penang, while adding to the continued transformation of The Light City into a fully integrated waterfront destination.

title: Jendela Residences clinches Top Development with 'semi-D in the sky' homes by the fairways
article:
Overlooking the championship fairways of the Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club and the greenery of Bukit Kiara Federal Park, Jendela Residences offers a rare kind of city living.

The 520-unit development by Sime Darby Property in KLGCC Resort was completed at the end of 2025, and every unit has since been sold.

Jendela Residences was named Top Development (Central Malaysia) in the high-rise category at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026, marking the developer’s first win at the awards.

Since completion, subsale prices have risen by about 30% above launch prices, and a waiting list of prospective buyers remains in place.

About 80% of the homes are owner-occupied, mostly by high-net-worth Malaysians from neighbourhoods such as Damansara Heights, TTDI, Mont Kiara and Petaling Jaya.

Some affluent families have bought multiple units to live close to one another while keeping their independence. The development has also drawn returning Malaysians and golfers looking for a retirement address.

In particular, residents will be able to appreciate the rare balance of lush greenery, championship golf and urban convenience, Sime Darby Property said.

Woven into nature

Designed by Triarch Architects, Jendela draws inspiration from the Malay weaving traditions of sulaman and anyaman , translating the craftsmanship of songket into a contemporary architectural language.

The weaving motif carries through to the landscape by Design INC, where striped paving, curving pool decks and layered planting create a resort-like setting.

Each typical floor has just four units per wing, with no intermediate units, creating a "semi-D in the sky".

The homes, comprising three-bedroom, three-bedroom-plus-study and four-bedroom-plus-study layouts, feature wide living and dining areas, wet and dry kitchens and balconies with views of the golf course, Bukit Kiara and the city skyline. Four units in Tower A come with private infinity pools.

Facilities include a 50m infinity pool overlooking the golf course, a yoga and pilates barn, sky lounge, infrared sauna, herb garden and a viewing pavilion.

Hotel-style living

Like a high-end hotel, Jendela separates its back-of-house operations from the areas used by residents and guests, with dedicated access for services, maintenance and waste collection. Car park ramps are wider to accommodate luxury and sports cars, while selected units come with storage lockers up to 3m tall.

The development is GreenRE Gold-certified. Low-E glass and solar blinds on west-facing balconies reduce heat gain, while solar panels, regenerative lifts and rainwater harvesting cut energy and water use.

Every unit’s car park bay is ready for an EV charger, and a complimentary shuttle service connects residents to nearby neighbourhoods.

A coveted address

Jendela’s appeal is closely tied to its setting. KLGCC Resort spans 360 acres, with only about 16% designated for development.

At its heart is the Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club, with 36 holes of championship golf and a history of hosting international tournaments, including 11 years of LPGA events.

The township has also grown into a lifestyle destination. KLGCC Mall opened in October 2025 with about 90% of its retail space committed, serving a catchment of more than 300,000 residents.

Together with The Courts, Menara KLGCC and the revitalised KLGCC Convention Centre, it brings shopping, dining and business spaces closer to home.

Limited land for residential development, coupled with a carefully curated collection of homes, means that ownership within KLGCC Resort remains a rare privilege.

What’s next

KLGCC Resort is preparing to launch its next residential project, with only limited development opportunities remaining in the township.

Designed as a transit-oriented development, it will centre on wellness, with biophilic architecture, restorative spaces and integrated greenery. It is aimed at affluent young professionals, multigenerational families and those planning an active retirement.

Sime Darby Property sees the EPEA win as an opportunity to introduce Jendela Residences and KLGCC Resort to a wider regional audience, including Malaysians living and working in Singapore.

The developer said that it has seen a “strong level of cross-border interest in Jendela Residences”. The recognition provides a timely platform on which to build momentum and showcase how the wider KLGCC Resort masterplan combines low-density luxury with long-term investment value, Sime Darby Property added.

The regional accolade adds to the developer’s domestic recognition. Sime Darby Property was named Malaysia’s No. 1 property developer at The Edge Malaysia Top Property Developers Awards 2025 for the second consecutive year.

title: Eden Taman Duta wins double honours for villa living in a forest setting
article:
Tucked into the rolling, forested hills of Taman Duta, one of Kuala Lumpur’s most exclusive enclaves, Eden Taman Duta is designed to feel like a canopy among the trees.

The freehold development by BRDB Developments comprises just 146 villa-style residences across eight low-density blocks, set within 12.25 acres of tropical gardens with views of the city skyline.

The project, which is scheduled to be completed by 2030, won two awards at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026: Top Development (Central Malaysia) and Top Luxury Development (Central Malaysia), both in the high-rise category.

"Winning both awards is a significant milestone for BRDB. It provides independent recognition of Eden Taman Duta’s overall proposition and introduces our work to a wider regional audience, including prospective buyers and industry stakeholders beyond Malaysia," says deputy CEO, Yasmin Khan.

The developer behind Bangsar Shopping Centre, The Troika, One Menerung and Serai has held the 12.25-acre site since 1997, and Eden Taman Duta is its final residential development in Taman Duta.

Every home has at least five bedrooms; the 6,491 sq ft Type C, for instance, has 4+2 bedrooms and six bathrooms. At the top are 22 limited-edition penthouses.

Landed living, reimagined

Rather than cut deep into the site’s natural valley, BRDB chose to build a continuous podium across it.

"Although this required a greater upfront investment, it allowed us to work with the land’s existing topography and create a more cohesive environment for residents," says Yasmin.

Designed by GDP Architects, the blocks adopt a contemporary tropical style, with clean lines, natural materials and large openings that draw in light, breezes and greenery. They are arranged in clusters with generous spacing and layered landscaping between them, preserving privacy while maximising views.

The heart of the development takes its cue from a water stream that once ran through the site. A central spine links the clubhouse, a 35m lap pool and the wellness pavilion, recreating the gentle flow of nature through the estate.

The homes are pitched at well-travelled buyers who are used to landed living. "Eden Taman Duta offers an alternative for those who wish to retain the space, privacy and sense of independence associated with a landed home, without the same responsibilities of maintaining a large property," says Yasmin.

Interiors by Edo Yvonne Design Assembly pair natural stone and timber with a soft, neutral palette. Dry kitchens feature Poggenpohl cabinetry and Gaggenau appliances, while wardrobes are by Molteni & C and bathrooms are fitted by Villeroy & Boch and Hansgrohe. The showroom was designed with SPACE Furniture Group.

"These specifications are integral to the homes rather than simply optional upgrades," she adds.

A private resort

The landscape by Walrus Design turns the estate into a resort-style retreat. Beyond a private, gated entrance, residents have access to a clubhouse with a concierge, lounges and a gym.

A walled, adults-only spa garden offers massage rooms, a sauna, steam room and an infinity-edge pool overlooking the rainforest canopy.

The car park roofs have been turned into gardens, with a tennis court set within a pergola-lined "lawn club" on one side and an al fresco grill pavilion on the other.

A rolling lawn with putting and chipping areas hosts festive gatherings, while terraced hanging gardens lead to pavilions cantilevered over a biodiversity terrace, entered through bio-filter pools that support native fish and aquatic plants.

Native Malaysian species dominate the planting, extending a green canopy from the neighbouring forest reserve into the estate and drawing birds and pollinators.

Solar panels, rainwater harvesting, regenerative lifts, LED lighting with smart controls and EV charging stations further reduce the development’s environmental footprint.

Looking ahead

BRDB believes the luxury market will continue to be shaped by discerning buyers who value location, privacy, design integrity and long-term value. Besides Eden Taman Duta, its pipeline includes developments in Bangsar and Permas Jaya. In Johor, its Emerald Bay project is set to target a wider regional audience, particularly Singapore buyers, on the back of improving cross-border connectivity.

"As we continue to advance our development pipeline, we will remain focused on delivering projects that are distinctive in their own context, commercially considered and built to retain their relevance over time," says Yasmin. "Ultimately, our ambition is to build a legacy that can be appreciated from one generation to the next."

title: Sapphire by the Gardens clinches Top Development with a landmark sky bridge over Melbourne
article:
Rising opposite Australia's Unesco World Heritage-listed Carlton Gardens, Sapphire by the Gardens has added a striking new silhouette to the Melbourne skyline.

Its twin glass towers, linked high above the city by a two-storey sky bridge, house 325 luxury residences alongside the five-star Shangri-La Melbourne hotel.

Developed by Selangor-headquartered S P Setia Bhd, through its subsidiary Setia (Melbourne) Development Co, the completed project was named Top Development (Australia) in the high-rise category at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026.

The project's success is also reflected in its sales. All 325 residences have been sold, generating about RM1.6 billion (around $500,000) in revenue, the developer says.

S P Setia acquired the 4,164 sq m (44,821 sq ft) corner site at 308 Exhibition Street from Australian telco group Telstra in 2016, following an international expression-of-interest exercise contested by other overseas developers.

It then held a design competition, which was won jointly by architecture firms COX and Fender Katsalidis Architects.

Construction began in April 2019 and, despite disruptions from the Covid-19 pandemic, the development was completed in about three and a half years, with practical completion achieved in stages up to July 2023.

It has a gross floor area of about 1.7 million sq ft. The residences range from one-bedroom units to penthouses, with two-bedroom and two-bedroom-plus-study units making up more than half of the mix.

Bridge in the sky

The two towers, of 60 and 62 storeys, rise above a nine-storey podium. The champagne -gold sky bridge that connects them features an oculus — a transparent, glass-floor cutout — at Level 46, and was the first of its kind in Australia at the time of construction.

The final design emerged from an internal competition between the two architecture firms, and installing the 2,368 sq ft structure at such a height was an engineering feat in itself.

For residents, the sky bridge is more than a link between towers. It is a vantage point, offering sweeping views of Carlton Gardens and the city beyond.

From the upper floors, residents can see across the Melbourne CBD to Port Phillip Bay and the Dandenong Ranges.

The penthouse on Level 57 set a record as the most expensive in Melbourne, fetching RM122 million. Spanning 1,200 sq m (about 12,900 sq ft) over two storeys, it made headlines when the buyer’s McLaren Senna GTR luxury car was lifted into the unit by crane.

Overcoming complex engineering

Below ground, the project confronted one of Melbourne’s toughest construction challenges.

The towers sit directly above active underground railway tunnels, requiring specialist structural engineering and precise construction sequencing throughout the construction.

The raft foundation was laid in what was then the largest single concrete pour in Melbourne’s history. The builder, Multiplex, poured 2,977 cubic metres of concrete over 24 hours, using 150 trucks that made 465 deliveries.

Multiplex has since been appointed by S P Setia to build Atlas Melbourne, its 73-storey residential tower on La Trobe Street. At the project’s groundbreaking in September, S P Setia chairman Syed Zainol Anwar Jamalullail noted that Multiplex had delivered Sapphire by the Gardens on time and within budget.

Garden at the doorstep

The design by landscape architect Taylor Cullity Lethlean draws the greenery of Carlton Gardens across the street and onto the podium, where planting cascades over terraced levels and recedes into the curved forms of the towers above.

At street level, a porte cochère serving hotel guests, residents and diners opens onto a green public forecourt. Through-site pedestrian links draw people into the heart of the precinct.

Inside, residents have access to an infinity pool, sky lounge, private dining room, cinema, karaoke room, sauna and gym, as well as a 24-hour concierge. An app lets residents book facilities and log maintenance requests.

Powered by green energy

Sapphire by the Gardens was one of the first buildings in Australia to be connected to green energy, with residents drawing on 100% green electricity at competitive prices. The commitment was made at the concept stage.

Rainwater is collected and reused on site, while the towers’ flowing curves were shaped to maximise sunlight and views while reducing wind at street level.

With trams, trains, shops, theatres and universities within a short walk, residents can also leave their cars at home.

With its landmark sky bridge, sold-out residences and engineering achievements, Sapphire by the Gardens has set a new benchmark for luxury living in Melbourne.

title: Best US Stocks to Buy Now: 5 S&P 500 Stocks That Could Be Bargains After the Sell-Off
article:
Fears over rising bond yields and the return on
AI investment
have pressured share prices, at least for some companies, creating uncertainty for investors.
However, market corrections can also provide opportunities to invest in quality businesses at more reasonable valuations.
The key is identifying companies with strong fundamentals, durable competitive advantages and attractive long-term growth prospects.
This article will take a closer look at five
S&P 500 stocks
that have suffered a decline of at least 10% over the past month (as at 30 October 2026).
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) – The Mega-Cap Growth Stock
Meta’s shares fell 15.3% in October, with investors concerned over the costs of its AI investments and legal troubles (the latter include a US$25 billion fine imposed by a judge in New Mexico).
Although investors were excited over the rapid uptake of Meta’s Muse agent, questions remain over whether the returns will justify the company’s massive AI investments.
In fact, the company’s recently released figures for 3Q2026 showed free cash flow going negative.
However, the company’s core advertising business is still going strong.
In 3Q2026, revenue grew 26% year on year, although the operating margin halved to 20%, partly because of legal costs.
Looking ahead, Meta’s ability to monetise its AI business remains key, and this will depend on how much value it can extract from consumers (from advertising, subscription fees, commissions etc.), and what percentage of its 3.6 billion daily active user base it can activate.
Meta also faces various legal and regulatory challenges, including the August 2026 agreement to resolve litigation related to teen mental health, which provides for US$18.6 billion in settlements.
These could end up becoming a recurring cost of doing business, and not just one-offs.
AT&T Inc (NYSE: T) – The Undervalued Consumer Giant
AT&T’s stock is down by 11.9% over the past month, amid concerns that
Starlink
, the satellite internet service of
SpaceX
(NASDAQ: SPCX), will muscle in on the telco business.
Despite the decline, the company’s business is performing decently, especially for a mature telco.
Overall revenue for the first 9 months of 2026 was 3.5% higher than a year earlier, reaching over US$95 billion.
Notably, its advanced connectivity segment, which aims to provide subscribers with both 5G and fibre coverage, is growing faster than the overall business.
The company expects to generate over US$18 billion in free cash flow in 2026, rising to over US$21 billion in 2028.
This will provide it with plenty to return to shareholders, whether in the form of dividends or share buybacks.
The telco is currently trading at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of just 8.3x, compared to 12.6x in March this year.
This could prove to be a bargain, but only if Starlink proves to be less of a threat than feared.
Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) – The AI / Semiconductor Opportunity
Micron, one of the big 3 memory
chipmakers
globally, has seen its shares fall by 19.4% over the past month, as investors question how sustainable the AI boom is.
This sell-off comes despite the company’s strong financial performance.
Revenue for its financial year ending September 2026 (FY2026) was up 256% to US$133 billion.
Net income rose to 9.1 times its FY2025 level, reaching US$87 billion.
The company expects its FY2027 performance to be even stronger, as industry demand has actually gone up over the past quarter.
However, many of these gains appear to be already priced in as Micron’s share price rose 884% between January 2025 and October 2026, making investors nervous at the slightest hint of turbulence in AI-driven demand.
There’s also the spectre of more competition.
Currently, the global market for memory chips is an oligopoly – Micron,
Samsung Electronics
(KRX: 005930) and
SK Hynix
(KRX: 000660) accounted for 87% of global DRAM market share in 2Q2026.
But new competitors, such as China’s
ChangXin Memory Technologies
(SSE: 688825), or CXMT, may disrupt the market, resulting in lower margins.
The Charles Schwab Corporation (NYSE: SCHW) – The Financial Blue Chip
Charles Schwab is a leading investment services firm with over US$13 trillion in client assets.
Its shares are down by over 10% in the past month.
The stock has declined, in part, because of fears that AI agents will be able to help investors trade, disrupting the business model of incumbents such as Charles Schwab.
The company continues to deliver strong financial performance.
Revenue of US$20.7 billion in the first nine months of 2026 (9M2026) was 18% higher than a year ago, while net income rose by 28% to US$8.1 billion.
Schwab is not waiting for AI to eat its lunch.
It recently launched Charley, an AI-powered assistant to provide clients with conversational access to tools and insights.
Schwab also serves Registered Investment Advisors (RIAs) in the US and has partnered with Anthropic to bring Claude to these RIAs.
These initiatives, along with its brand name and long track record, should enable Schwab to adapt and thrive in this new AI era.
Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOG) – The Quality Compounder
Alphabet has declined by 16.9% over the past month, as investors grew concerned about its high AI spend, as well as the cannibalisation of its higher-margin search business by its lower-margin AI search feature.
Alphabet reported negative free cash flow (FCF) of US$9.1 billion in 3Q2026, its second consecutive quarter in the red.
However, top-line growth is actually accelerating.
In 3Q2026, revenue was 25% higher than a year ago, compared to 16% in 3Q2025.
If the company is able to keep growing revenue, this might offset margin declines, allowing the absolute level of profits to continue rising.
Alphabet remains one of the best-placed enterprises to navigate the AI era, with a unique combination of cloud, AI, and advertising businesses that can benefit from the technology.
One potential game-changer that the market may not be paying enough attention to is its business selling tensor processing unit (TPU) chips, its homegrown AI chip system, which was once reserved for internal use but is now being sold directly to customers.
The value of the TPU business has been estimated at US$900 billion, which would make a meaningful contribution to Alphabet’s current US$3.4 trillion market capitalisation.

title: STI’s Red October 2026: 4 Blue-Chip REITs Still in the Green
article:
Singaporeans know how it feels when the transboundary haze settles over the island.
October brought a different kind of haze for investors, as Singapore’s blue chips came under pressure.
But four
real estate investment trusts
(REITs) managed to rise above the gloom, delivering positive returns despite the downturn.
The
SPDR STI ETF
(SGX: ES3), an ETF that mimics Singapore’s
Straits Times Index
(SGX: ^STI), delivered a negative 5.5% return for October 2026.
Over the same period,
Frasers Centrepoint Trust
(SGX: J69U), or FCT, delivered a 3.5% total return.
CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust
(SGX: C38U), or CICT,
Frasers Logistics & Commercial Trust
(SGX: BUOU), or FLCT, and
Mapletree Logistics Trust
(SGX: M44U), or MLT, returned 2.2%, 1.7% and 0.9%, respectively.

Source: Fiscal.ai.
These are total returns, which include distributions and not just unit price movements.
The gains may appear modest, but they still stand in stark contrast to the STI’s dip.
So what helped them weather the
downturn
?
Their latest business updates offer some clues.
What drove FCT’s record payout?
FCT
owns a portfolio of eight suburban malls in Singapore.
For the fiscal year ended 30 September 2026 (FY2026), net property income (NPI) rose 15.7% year on year (YoY) to S$321.7 million.
A full year’s contribution from Northpoint City’s South Wing provided the biggest boost.
Distribution per unit (DPU) climbed 2.0% to a record S$0.12350, while second-half DPU grew 2.6% YoY to S$0.06214.
Retail committed occupancy stood at 99.7%, excluding NEX, which is currently undergoing an asset enhancement initiative (AEI).
Rental reversions came in at 6.6%, while the average cost of debt fell to 3.2% from 3.8% a year ago.
However, the results were not entirely rosy.
Distributions from joint ventures fell 11.7% YoY, as a one-off special distribution from the previous year did not recur.
Tenant sales growth was also modest at just 1.3%.
Where is Singapore’s largest REIT finding growth?
CICT had a strong third quarter of 2026 (3Q2026), with NPI rising 13.8% YoY to S$334.9 million.
As CICT pays distributions half-yearly, there was no DPU this quarter.
New assets drove the growth.
CICT acquired Paragon on 1 July 2026, while Gallileo in Frankfurt and its increased stake in CapitaSpring also contributed to the stronger performance.
Integrated development NPI climbed 40.8% YoY.
There were also some encouraging signs across the portfolio.
Committed occupancy improved from 95.6% to 96.1% over the quarter, while nine-month rental reversions came in at 4.6% for retail and 7.1% for office properties.
The average cost of debt also eased to 2.8%.
However, not everything was moving in the right direction.
Retail NPI fell 8.2% YoY, while aggregate leverage climbed to 39.7%.
Can logistics make up for FLCT’s business park problem?
FLCT has 114 properties spread across five countries.
It reports financial results only twice a year, so its latest business update for the third quarter of the fiscal year ending 30 September 2026 (3QFY2026) did not include NPI or DPU figures.
Overall portfolio occupancy was 96.1%, while its logistics and industrial (L&I) business was a bright spot, with occupancy at 99.7%.
Rental reversions for these properties also came in at a healthy 11.9%.
The trust also expanded its logistics portfolio, acquiring four freehold properties in Germany and the Netherlands for around S$441.5 million.
Management expects the deal to lift DPU by 1.7%.
But the picture was less encouraging for its commercial properties.
Commercial rental reversions were -0.3%, while nine leases at Alexandra Technopark were renewed at rents 3.6% below their previous rates.
For now, FLCT’s L&I properties appear to be doing the heavy lifting.
Is China still weighing on MLT?
MLT owns 172 logistics properties, but its latest results point to relatively modest growth.
For the second quarter of the fiscal year ending 31 March 2027 (2QFY2027), NPI rose 1.0% YoY to S$154.8 million, while DPU edged up 0.1% to S$0.01816.
There was some improvement in rental reversions, which picked up to 2.1% from 0.9% in the previous quarter.
However, China remained a weak spot, with rental reversions still at -1.7%, compared with 4.2% excluding China.
MLT also divested around S$243 million worth of assets during the current fiscal year, at an average 3.1% premium to valuation.
Distributions to perpetual securities holders rose 33.6% YoY.
Aggregate leverage fell to 37.5% from 40.5%, although this was partly due to MLT temporarily using proceeds from perpetual securities to repay debt.
What did these four REITs have in common?
Occupancy across all four portfolios stayed above 96%, while rental reversions were positive in most parts of their portfolios.
Asset sales tested valuations.
FLCT sold its long-vacant Juniper building 37.5% above book value, and MLT’s divestments fetched a premium.
To put it simply, these REITs kept most of their buildings full and most of their rents rising.
In a volatile month, that may have given investors some reassurance.
Get Smart: Ask how the next deal gets paid for
One month of outperformance tells you little about the next twelve.
Gearing, however, offers clearer information.
FCT’s White Sands proceeds will cut aggregate leverage from 38.7% to 36.8%.
The other three REITs are closer to the 40% mark.
CICT’s aggregate leverage stands at 39.7%, while MLT’s pro forma gearing, which assumes the November 2026 redemption of its older perpetual securities, would be 40.4%.
FLCT’s leverage will reach about 38.7% once its acquisition settles.
That leaves S$547 million of headroom, down from S$727 million a quarter ago.
But why does this matter?
A REIT with limited borrowing headroom may need to issue new units to fund its next acquisition.
New units can dilute DPU.
Before you buy any of them, check the gearing and ask how management plans to pay for the next deal.

title: AI elite lose US$18 bil as chip stock rout spreads to Asia
article:
(Nov 6): SoftBank Group Corp founder Masayoshi Son and other tycoons across Asia saw billions erased from their fortunes as a global tech sell-off rippled through their companies on Friday.

Twenty-two billionaires from China, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea who rank in the world’s 500 richest lost more than US$21 billion ($27 billion) in combined wealth as of 10am Hong Kong time, before paring that to more than US$18 billion, according to calculations from the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Son was the biggest loser, with his fortune declining by US$3.9 billion to about US$29 billion.

Among the hardest hit were the firms at the heart of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. Those who lost US$1 billion or more include Takemitsu Takizaki of electronic sensor maker Keyence Corp, and Singapore’s richest person Jason Chang of ASE Technology Holding Co, which assembles and packages semiconductors.

Samsung Electronics Co shareholders Jay Y Lee, his mother and sister — one of Asia’s richest families — collectively lost about US$2.5 billion from their fortunes.

The turmoil also last month hit hedge funds including Tiger Global Management and Whale Rock Capital Management, as concerns over AI investments roiled markets. In Asia, wealthy clients of brokers from Taiwan to Hong Kong faced margin calls on leveraged bets, people familiar with the matter said.

Expectations that a Democrat-controlled House of Representatives and Senate will work to slow construction of data centres — a critical component of AI infrastructure — helped drive technology stocks lower across Asia on Friday, following a record US$2.3 trillion wipeout in market value of the Nasdaq 100 index. The losses extended a wealth reversal that saw Nvidia Corp’s Jensen Huang drop out of the world’s top 10 richest.
